DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'The hosted Sentry MCP needs a token scoped to read issues, events, and projects.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Log in to Sentry and open **User Auth Tokens**:
https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/
- Click **Create New Token** and give it a name like `holmes-mcp`.
- Grant these read scopes: `org:read`, `project:read`, `event:read`.
- Copy the token now - Sentry only shows it once.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry token in the robusta namespace so the Holmes pod can read it.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token=<PASTE_YOUR_SENTRY_TOKEN>', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this snippet into your existing generated_values.yaml (do not create a new file).', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token

  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry error monitoring - read issues, events, and projects"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      icon_url: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/sentry/362D59"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use Sentry
        Use Sentry whenever investigating **application errors, exceptions, crashes, or regressions**, especially when correlating a Kubernetes symptom (pod restarts, 5xx spikes, elevated error rates) with an application-level stack trace.

        ## Preferred tools
        - **List projects** with `find_projects` (or the equivalent list-projects tool) to discover which Sentry project a service maps to.
        - **Search / list issues** with `find_issues` / `search_issues`, filtered by project and time range, to find the top errors or a specific issue.
        - **Read issue details and events** with `get_issue_details` / `get_event_details` to retrieve the exception type, message, stack trace, and affected releases/environments.

        ## Rules
        - Read-only only. Do **not** call any tool that resolves, assigns, comments on, or otherwise mutates a Sentry issue.
        - Always scope queries by `organization_slug` and `project_slug` when known, and by a tight time window that matches the incident.
'}, {'label': 'Apply the change', 'detail': 'Upgrade Robusta with your updated values. Holmes will restart automatically.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=prod', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Sentry shows up as a data source and that Holmes can call it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod to become Ready.
- Open the Robusta UI **Data Sources** page and confirm **Sentry** (key `sentry-custom`) appears as enabled.
- Ask Holmes something like: *"List my Sentry projects"* or *"Show the top unresolved issues in project X in the last 24h"* and confirm real data comes back.
- If it fails with `401 Unauthorized`, re-check the token scopes (`org:read`, `project:read`, `event:read`) and that the secret `sentry-mcp-token` exists in the `robusta` namespace.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'Generate a personal auth token in Sentry with read scopes for issues and projects.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Open Sentry: https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/
- Click **Create New Token**
- Give it a name (e.g. `holmes-mcp`)
- Grant the following read scopes: `org:read`, `project:read`, `event:read`, `member:read`, `team:read`
- Save and copy the token value (starts with `sntryu_...`) - you will paste it into the Kubernetes secret in the next step
- Docs: https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret with your Sentry token', 'detail': 'Stores your Sentry User Auth Token so the Robusta runner can read it at runtime.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token=<PASTE_YOUR_SENTRY_TOKEN_HERE>', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Merge the Sentry MCP values into generated_values.yaml', 'detail': "Adds Sentry as a remote MCP server pointing at Sentry's vendor-hosted endpoint.", 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry MCP server - read issues, errors, and projects from Sentry."
      icon_url: "https://s1.sentry-cdn.com/_static/dc7b6598d1cffdaef27b1ec72c6c92b1/sentry/images/favicon.ico"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use Sentry
        Use this data source whenever the user asks about **application errors, exceptions, crashes, or issue triage** captured by Sentry, or when correlating a Kubernetes alert (crashloops, 5xx spikes) with recent Sentry issues in the affected service.

        ## What Holmes should do
        - **List projects** to discover which Sentry project matches the service in question - do this first when the project slug is unknown.
        - **Search / list issues** in a project (filter by `is:unresolved`, environment, or a time window) to find the most recent or most frequent errors.
        - **Fetch issue details and events** (stack traces, breadcrumbs, tags, release, environment) to explain the root cause and cite exact error messages.

        ## Guidelines
        - Prefer **read-only** Sentry tools; do not resolve, assign, or mutate issues unless the user explicitly asks.
        - Always include the Sentry **organization slug** and **project slug** when the tool requires them.
        - Quote the exact error message, event ID, and first-seen / last-seen timestamps when reporting findings.'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Rolls out the updated Robusta runner with the Sentry MCP server enabled.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=prod', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify Sentry is connected', 'detail': 'Confirm the new data source is live and Holmes can call it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Robusta/Holmes pods to restart in the `robusta` namespace
- Open the **Data Sources** page in Robusta and confirm **Sentry** (key `sentry-custom`) appears as connected
- Ask Holmes: *"List my Sentry projects"* - a successful reply confirms the token and endpoint are working
- Then try: *"Show the latest unresolved Sentry issues for project <your-project-slug>"*', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry auth token', 'detail': 'Generate a User Auth Token in Sentry with read scopes for org, projects, issues and events.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Open Sentry and go to **Settings → Account → User Auth Tokens** (or **Settings → Auth Tokens** for org tokens).
- Click **Create New Token**.
- Grant these read scopes at minimum:
  - `org:read`
  - `project:read`
  - `event:read`
  - `issue:read`
- Copy the token now (it will not be shown again).

Docs:
https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/
https://docs.sentry.io/account/auth-tokens/', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry token in the robusta namespace so the runner can read it.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='YOUR_SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this into your existing generated_values.yaml under holmes.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry MCP server - read Sentry issues, errors and projects for triage"
      icon_url: "https://sentry.io/_assets/logos/sentry-glyph.svg"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use
        Use this when the user asks about **Sentry** errors, exceptions, crashes, issues, releases, or wants to see which Sentry projects exist in the organization. Also use it to enrich Kubernetes / application incidents with application-level error context from Sentry.

        ## What to do
        - To list projects: call the Sentry MCP `find_projects` / `list_projects` tool (whichever is exposed) for the relevant organization slug.
        - To find issues / errors: use `find_issues` / `search_issues` scoped by `organization_slug` and `project_slug`; filter by query (e.g. `is:unresolved`), and by time range when the user gives one.
        - To inspect a specific error: use `get_issue_details` / `get_issue_summary` / `get_event_details` with the Sentry issue id or short id (e.g. `PROJECT-123`).

        ## Rules
        - **Read-only.** Only call read / list / get tools. Do NOT resolve, assign, delete, mutate, or create anything in Sentry.
        - Always ask the user for the `organization_slug` / `project_slug` if it is not obvious from context.
        - Prefer narrow queries (specific project + short time window) over broad org-wide scans.'}, {'label': 'Apply the changes', 'detail': 'Run the Helm upgrade to reload Holmes with the new data source.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=prod', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Sentry shows up as a data source and Holmes can query it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and for the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart and become Ready.
- Open Holmes and check the **Data Sources** list - a `sentry-custom` entry (labelled Sentry) should appear as connected.
- Ask Holmes something like:
  - `List my Sentry projects`
  - `Show unresolved Sentry issues in project <your-project-slug> from the last 24 hours`
- If it fails to authenticate, re-check the secret contents and that the token has the required read scopes.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})
